title: SILG Remulla on hunt for Zaldy, Bato, Atong, Bantag: Good results will come soon
summary: Interior and Local Government Secretary Jonvic Remulla on Monday said authorities are continuing operations to locate and arrest high-profile fugitives, expressing hope that there would be…

blocks.text: Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG) Secretary Jonvic Remulla on Monday said authorities are continuing operations to locate and arrest high-profile fugitives, expressing hope that there would be developments before the end of the year.

"Well, we're at it. The operations continue. Makakaasa kayo (Rest assured) that good results will come soon," Remulla told reporters in an ambush interview when asked for updates on the government's efforts to track down the fugitives.
Asked whether authorities could make progress before the year ends, Remulla replied, "Sana (Hopefully)."

Among the high-profile fugitives being pursued by authorities are former lawmaker Zaldy Co, Senator Ronald "Bato" dela Rosa, businessman Charlie "Atong" Ang, and former Bureau of Corrections (BuCor) chief Gerald Bantag.

The Office of the Ombudsman has charged Co and several former Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) officials over alleged irregularities in a P289-million road dike project in Naujan, Oriental Mindoro.

Dela Rosa is wanted by the International Criminal Court (ICC) in connection with the crimes against humanity case stemming from former president Rodrigo Duterte's war on drugs. The senator, who was the Philippine National Police chief during Duterte's term as president, is accused of being a co-perpetrator in the alleged crimes.
A P50-million reward is being offered for information that would lead to the senator's arrest.

Authorities are also searching for Ang, who remains the only accused still at large in connection with the missing sabungeros case. Arrest warrants have been issued against Ang and other accused over multiple counts of kidnapping with homicide and kidnapping and serious illegal detention.
A P10-million reward is offered for information on Ang's whereabouts.
Bantag, meanwhile, is wanted in connection with the death of Jun Villamor, the alleged middleman in the October 2022 killing of broadcaster Percy Lapid.
A Muntinlupa Regional Trial Court ordered Bantag's arrest in April 2023.
A P2-million reward is also offered for information that would lead to Bantag's arrest. —KG, GMA News
